home.title: Know your crop's grade and fair price before you sell.
home.lede: Take a photo of your dates, melons or grain. Dera Mandi grades it, shows what buyers pay for that grade, and finds buyers, storage and transport near you.
home.why: Dhakki dates from D.I. Khan reach the Gulf and beyond, yet growers often sell to the first commission agent at the price he names, because the fruit will not keep and there is no fair price to point to.
home.step1d: One to three photos, in daylight.
home.step2: See its grade and fair price
home.step2d: Grade A, B or C, and the price band buyers pay for it.
home.step3d: Pick a buyer, and a truck or cold store near you.

about.title: How Dera Mandi works
about.lede: A tool for growers in Dera Ismail Khan to know what their crop is worth before they sell it.
about.problem1: D.I. Khan grows export-grade Dhakki dates and Kulachi melons, along with wheat and sugarcane. The value leaks out before it reaches the grower, for three linked reasons.
about.problemPrice: Price is opaque. Most growers sell to a commission agent at the local mandi, under time pressure, at the price the agent names.
about.problemSpoil: Fruit spoils. There is little cold storage and the road to Multan or Karachi is long, so fruit is sold fast and cheap, or rots.
about.problemLots: Small lots cannot reach export. One grower rarely has enough graded fruit to interest an exporter, so the export premium goes to middlemen.
about.steps1: The grower photographs the crop and enters the quantity and village.
about.steps2: The app grades it A, B or C and shows the price band buyers pay for that grade.
about.steps3: It lists buyers who take that crop, grade and quantity, and nearby storage and transport, with cold storage first for fruit.
about.steps4: The grower picks a buyer and sends a request.
about.gradeTitle: How the grade is worked out
about.grade1: For khajoor, the grade comes from an image model (MobileNetV2) trained on {{trained}} photos of graded Pakistani khajoor from a public dataset. On {{tested}} photos of the three-grade varieties that it had never seen, it gave the right grade {{accuracy}}% of the time (95% range {{low}} to {{high}}%). Always guessing the most common grade would score {{baseline}}%. On a khajoor variety it never trained on (Fasli Toto, all labelled Grade 1), it said A for {{unseenA}}% of them. It runs on the phone; photos are never uploaded.
about.grade2: Its limits, plainly: the dataset shows Gajar, Kupro and Aseel khajoor, photographed one fruit at a time under a ring light. It has no Dhakki, and no piles photographed in a field, so accuracy on real field photos will be lower until Dhakki photos are added. Middle grade (B) is the hardest for it. The crop is still checked in person before anything is shipped.
about.grade3: For melons, wheat, sugarcane and other crops there is no graded photo set yet, so the grade is a rule-based estimate from colour, size and visible spots, not a trained model. If a photo is too dark, washed out, or does not show the crop, the app asks for a retake instead of guessing.
about.grade4: Next step: collect 100 to 300 graded Dhakki photos from D.I. Khan growers and retrain the same model on them.
about.lots1: Dera Mandi's plan is to combine nearby lots of the same crop and grade until they reach the size an exporter buys. In this prototype, that shows as a note on the result screen when a lot is too small.
about.realTitle: What is real in this prototype
about.real1: Real: the full listing flow, the trained khajoor grade model, photo checks, price bands, matching by crop, grade, quantity and distance, requests, and history, in Urdu and English.
about.real2: Sample: every buyer, store and transporter is an invented sample provider, not a real business. Prices are illustrative, not live mandi rates. A request is saved on the phone but does not reach anyone.
about.real3: Your listings and photos are kept only in this phone's browser. Nothing is uploaded.
about.faq1q: What if a grower cannot read or has no smartphone?
about.faq1a: The app opens in Urdu, uses large simple steps and crop pictures, and needs no account. One literate helper in a village can list crops for many growers.
about.faq2q: Why trust a grade from a photo?
about.faq2a: The photos stay with the listing so anyone can check them, and the crop is inspected in person before shipment. The grade is a fair starting point for the conversation, not a final verdict.
about.faq3q: Cold storage barely exists in D.I. Khan.
about.faq3a: True. Pooling demand from many growers is what makes shared storage worth building, and meanwhile the app routes toward existing cold hubs in Multan and Karachi.
about.team: Built for Imaginathon by Banao by The Four Musketeers.
about.credit: Training data: Maitlo, A. K. et al., Date Fruit Dataset for Inspection and Grading, Mendeley Data, V3 (2023), doi:10.17632/s5zfvsw5kv.3, licensed CC BY 4.0. Only the original photos were used; duplicates were removed and photos were cropped and resized for training and for the in-app samples.
about.grade1Dhakki: For khajoor, the grade comes from an image model (MobileNetV2) trained on {{trained}} graded khajoor photos: a public Pakistani dataset plus Dhakki photographed and graded in D.I. Khan. On {{tested}} Dhakki photos it had never seen, it gave the right grade {{accuracy}}% of the time (95% range {{low}} to {{high}}%). Always guessing the most common grade would score {{baseline}}%. It runs on the phone; photos are never uploaded.
about.grade2Dhakki: Its limits, plainly: the Dhakki test set is small ({{tested}} photos), so the true accuracy could sit anywhere in that range. Its training photos show one fruit at a time on a plain background, so piles and field light may score lower. Middle grade (B) is the hardest for it. The crop is still checked in person before anything is shipped.

rates.title: Mandi prices
rates.lede: Daily rates from AMIS Punjab (the government's Agriculture Marketing Information Service), nearest markets to D.I. Khan first. AMIS does not cover D.I. Khan itself or Dhakki dates, so you can type in your own mandi's rate for any crop.
rates.mine: You entered this rate on {{date}}. All bands and offers for this crop use it.
rates.reference: No public rate for this crop: these are illustrative prices.
rates.thirds: Grade C is the bottom third of this range, B the middle third, A the top third.
rates.noDhakki: AMIS lists Aseel and Irani dates, not Dhakki. Enter your mandi's Dhakki rate for a closer price.
rates.error: Enter a lowest and a highest rate, with the highest bigger than the lowest.
